claims.text: Integrating an ML potential, active learning, and on-the-fly ab initio reweighting will enable accurate high-temperature free energies for both solid and liquid phases.
The proposed workflow will retain vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The workflow will be 10- to 100-fold faster than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The workflow will outperform TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems.
The proposed framework combines active selection of critical configurations, on-the-fly ab initio recalibration, thermodynamic integration, and reweighting.
The method is intended to apply across elemental metals, binary alloys, and multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The method is intended for temperatures near melting transitions.
Anharmonic and electron–vibration effects are pronounced near melting.
A machine-learning interatomic potential can accurately emulate an ab initio potential-energy landscape in a multicomponent refractory high-entropy alloy.
The ML potential can accurately incorporate anharmonicity, vibrational entropy, and electron–vibration coupling.
Periodic recalibration using sparse ab initio evaluations captures the essential free-energy contributions without full ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling.
Enhanced sampling permits accurate integration over thermal fluctuations and preserves fidelity to ab initio free energies.
Predicted solid and liquid free energies will be within approximately 5% relative error of explicit ab initio MD benchmarks.
Predicted melting points and latent heats will be within approximately 5% relative error of explicit ab initio MD benchmarks.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics provides accurate reference results for fusion thermodynamics.
TOR-TILD is accurate for elemental and binary systems.
TOR-TILD becomes computationally prohibitive for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Vibrational entropy contributes to thermodynamic stabilization in a multicomponent CoCrFeNiTa alloy system.
The decisive benchmark will compare ML, explicit ab initio MD, and TOR-TILD results for solid–liquid free-energy differences, melting temperatures, latent heats, and thermal-expansion coefficients.
A relative error greater than 5% in free energies or derived properties over the tested range will falsify the hypothesis.
